svg.title: No fate but what we make
svg.desc: Four defense layers reduce agentic risk: scoped identity and trust, reviewed instructions and constrained tools, edit and runtime monitoring, and containment followed by evidence-preserving recovery. Short-lived credentials do not remove persistent instructions.
svg.text: No fate but what we make
Four boring layers against familiar failure modes · reduce exposure, constrain damage, verify recovery

g.text: IDENTITY — limit access and trust
Short-lived, scoped credentials · restrict OIDC trust to approved repos, branches and environments
Inventory non-human identities · protect credential issuers · review who can change trust
REDUCES CREDENTIAL EXPOSURE
short-lived keys do not erase implants
REVIEW AGENT TEXT — CONSTRAIN ITS TOOLS
Version and review instructions, memory writes, prompt templates and tool configs
Enforce least privilege, approval gates and egress limits outside the model
LIMITS THE BLAST RADIUS
review alone is not a security boundary
DETECT EDITS AND EXECUTION
Correlate workflow, webhook and memory edits with approved changes and runtime activity
Monitor tool calls, inference rates, egress and spend · triage drift · test the response
IMPROVES DETECTION
usage alerts are not hard spending caps
CONTAIN — THEN RECOVER
Contain active workers and identities · revoke sessions · preserve evidence · disable reactivation
Check queues and triggers · clean memory · restore reviewed state · verify before resuming
REDUCES REACTIVATION RISK
rotation alone does not finish recovery
None of this is exotic — boring, on purpose. Boring is the match for a threat built from familiar components.
1984's version needed a time machine and a factory. 2026's needs a stolen key, a retry loop, and one org that never reviewed the files its agents read.
